steps.name: Low-count filter, TMM normalization, and limma-voom differential expression (case vs control)
caveats: In a population cohort the sample-to-sample variation does not obey the negative binomial model; DESeq2 and edgeR can report many false positives even on permuted labels at n>=50/group. limma-voom keeps FDR closer to nominal but not universally — report a Wilcoxon or permutation check as a control.
steps.question: With filterByExpr low-count filtering and TMM normalization on the 12000 x 120 gene-level Salmon counts, which genes are differentially expressed between case (n=60) and control (n=60) whole-blood samples under a limma-voom fixed-effects model, given that at 60 samples/group the negative-binomial count models (DESeq2/edgeR) are known to exaggerate false positives?

grounding.reason: Population-scale cohort (60/60): rule R-0015 flags count-model false-positive inflation and mandates limma-voom with a stated Wilcoxon/permutation control; template tpl-limma-voom-fixed@1.0.0

acceptance_criteria: Genes filtered with filterByExpr (edgeR), minimum 10 counts in at least 60 samples (smallest group size)
TMM normalization factors computed with edgeR calcNormFactors before voom
voom precision weights computed and limma linear model fit with condition as an explicit factor, reference level (control) stated
Named contrast case-vs-control reported; moderated t-statistics and BH-adjusted p-values (alpha=0.05) reported for every tested gene
p-value histogram inspected and reported before trusting adjusted p-values

Caveat stated: population-scale cohort inflates false positives in count-based models; limma-voom chosen per the recommendation, and a Wilcoxon rank-sum test run as a control/sensitivity check on the same contrast
Number of genes tested and number of significant genes (padj<0.05) reported with effect sizes (logFC) alongside p-values

steps.name: WGCNA signed co-expression network, module detection, and module-trait correlation
caveats: A single-batch, unpaired 60 vs 60 design supports this network construction, but module-trait correlation is descriptive/exploratory — it is not a hypothesis test with the same guarantees as the differential expression model, and modules should be cross-checked against the limma-voom DE gene list for convergent evidence.
steps.question: Across all 120 whole-blood samples, what co-expression modules do the ~12000 genes (after low-count filtering) form under a signed WGCNA network, and which of these modules' eigengenes correlate significantly with case-vs-control status?

grounding.reason: Co-expression modules: signed WGCNA network on the variance-stabilized matrix, soft threshold by scale-free fit, eigengenes against traits, hubs by module membership, per R-0139@0008; template tpl-wgcna-modules@1.0.0

acceptance_criteria: Input is the vst-blind variance-stabilized expression matrix (from T1S1) restricted to the same low-count-filtered gene set used in T1S2
Soft-threshold power selected as the lowest power reaching scale-free topology fit index >= 0.8 (pickSoftThreshold), power and fit reported
Signed network built (blockwiseModules or equivalent step-wise TOM + hierarchical clustering) with minModuleSize=30 and mergeCutHeight=0.25 explicitly stated
Module eigengenes computed for every module (including grey/unassigned reported separately)
Each module eigengene correlated with case/control status (point-biserial/Pearson correlation with a p-value), multiple-testing correction across modules applied (BH)
Top hub genes per significant module ranked by module membership (kME, correlation of gene with its module eigengene) reported

Module count, module sizes, and sample size (n=120) stated beside every module correlation, with an explicit caution that correlations are estimated from 120 samples and can be unstable for small modules

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of case-associated modules and the DE gene ranking
steps.question: Which MSigDB Hallmark (and, as a follow-up, Reactome) gene sets are enriched among the genes of the WGCNA modules found to be significantly correlated with case/control status, and among the full ranked list of tested genes from the limma-voom contrast?

grounding.reason: Population-scale cohort enrichment: camera on the limma-voom fit as first pass, Hallmark then Reactome as collections, tested-gene universe, ORA gated at >=50 significant genes per R-0103; template tpl-camera-hallmark@1.0.0

acceptance_criteria: camera (limma) run on the full ranked gene list from T1S2 (ranked by moderated t-statistic) against MSigDB Hallmark (2026.1, human, 50 sets) with inter-gene correlation estimated from the data; universe = tested genes only

For each module significantly correlated with status in T2S1, an over-representation test (with the tested-gene universe) is run only if the module holds >=50 genes; otherwise state the module size and skip ORA per the small-list rule
Gene set size window applied: keep sets with 15-500 members among tested genes
Second pass against Reactome pathways (current release) reported for the same ranked list, with each collection's release stated and never merged into one set list
Gene identifiers mapped from symbol to Entrez via org.Hs.eg.db (version stated) before the ORA test; unmapped share reported
Redundant significant gene sets collapsed to one representative with members retained in a supplementary table
Report states that enrichment results are method-dependent (camera vs ORA can disagree) and gives both where applicable

plan.title: Whole-blood co-expression modules vs case/control status
plan.analytical_narrative: This 60 vs 60 human whole-blood cohort (raw Salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes x 120 samples, single batch, unpaired) asks which co-expression modules the genes form and which track case vs control. The core analysis is a WGCNA signed co-expression network built from the variance-stabilized, blind-transformed expression matrix: pick a soft-threshold power by the scale-free topology fit (~0.8), cluster genes into modules by topological overlap with dynamic tree cutting, compute module eigengenes, and correlate each eigengene with case/control status (module-trait correlation) plus report hub genes by module membership (kME). QC sample structure (PCA/heatmap on vst-blind values) runs first to confirm no batch/outlier structure would confound module detection or the trait correlation. Because each group has 60 samples (population-scale cohort), the knowledge base flags that DESeq2/edgeR's negative-binomial assumption is exaggerated at this size and recommends limma-voom with TMM normalization for a complementary differential-expression view of individual genes, feeding a camera/fgsea gene-set enrichment against MSigDB Hallmark (then Reactome) to interpret which pathways the case-associated modules and individual DE genes represent. A final report step ties module-trait results, hub genes, DE genes, and enrichment together with full reproducibility records (session info, seed, package/collection versions) and states the population-cohort caveat explicitly.
